pr.body:
Fixes #355

**What.** `compileHDL` step 4 recorded producers with `producerOf.set(signal, i)`, which overwrites, so a signal assembled from several slice writes only forced its *last* writer to run before the read. The earlier writers could be scheduled after it, and the read saw a half-assembled value — silently. `producersOf` now maps a signal to **every** part that writes it and the read takes an edge from each, so the topological order covers all of them.

**Repro, derived here rather than taken from the spike** (`src/core/hdl/compiler.test.ts`): a four-part chip where `t` is assembled from `t[0]` and `t[1]` and then read whole by `Not16`, with the `t[0]` writer made to depend on a third part so that permuting the parts really does permute the topological order. With `a=0`, `t = 0b11` and the correct `out` is `~3 & 0xffff = 65532`. Before the fix, the orderings `tLow,read,tHigh,k` and `tLow,tHigh,read,k` gave **65533** (bit 0 lost) while `read,tHigh,k,tLow` gave **65532** — the same 65533/65532 the spike measured. All 24 orderings now agree on 65532.

**Same-slice-twice: a compile error** (`Signal "t" bit 0 is driven by more than one part`), not last-wins-with-a-warning. Three reasons: two parts driving one bit is a short circuit, not a value; last-wins would preserve exactly the order-dependence this PR removes, since which write survived would still depend on the part order; and it is what the reference simulator does (`Cannot write to pin x[i] multiple times`, `../web-ide/simulator/src/chip/builder.ts`). `HDLCompileResult` has no warning channel, and adding one for this would have been new surface area for a case that is never meaningful. Overlap is checked in both directions, so a whole-signal write that overlaps a slice write is rejected too; disjoint slice writes are unaffected.

**Deviation — the property test does not use `fast-check`.** The issue says it "is already a dependency"; it is not, in `package.json` or the lockfile. Introducing it is #198's job, so per AGENTS.md §1.0 ("trust the code over the ticket") the property is expressed with an exhaustive permutation sweep plus a seeded `mulberry32` sample, no new dependency. The generator puts writers at *mixed* dependency depths on purpose: a generator with every writer at the same depth is vacuous here, because Kahn's queue happens to drain them all before the reader whatever the source order — measured on the unfixed compiler, uniform depth 1 gave 0/400 wrong permutations and mixed depths 0–2 gave 105/400. Recommend moving these two tests to `fast-check` when #198 lands.

**Project-1 vectors still pass** — `src/core/testing/{engine,implementationSources}.test.ts` and `src/core/hdl/project1-bottom-up.test.ts`, 66 tests, green; no Project-1 chip drives a bit twice.

**Follow-up filed:** #361 — the total width of a slice-assembled signal is never inferred, so an unsliced read of one is not width-checked. Adjacent, not fixed here.
